anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the two 4-pin fan headers are wired with the 12 V feed on the top (first) pin: the +12V symbol/node (same rail as the barrel jack, D7 and U5 IN1) is wired down into pin 1 of J7 and J8 (Conn_01x04_Pin), while pin 2 of each connector is wired to the GND symbol below the headers. Pin 3 of J7 carries FAN_0_TACH and pin 3 of J8 carries FAN_1_TACH; pin 4 of each is left no-connect.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the fan-header 12 V pins are pin 2 of each header ('the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)'), i.e. pin 1 = GND, pin 2 = +12 V, pin 3 = tach, pin 4 = NC — the standard 4-pin fan pinout. If the +12 V feed is on pin 1, then pin 2 is ground and the two supply pins of the header are effectively reversed.

evidence.quote: and the two fan-header 12 V pins (`J7`/`J8` pin 2)
Power sheet: +12V symbol wired to first pin of J7/J8 (Conn_01x04_Pin); GND symbol wired to second pin of J7/J8; FAN_0_TACH on J7 pin 3, FAN_1_TACH on J8 pin 3

anomalies.impact: A fan plugged into either header using the standard pinout receives reversed supply polarity (12 V applied to its ground lead, ground on its +12 V lead). The fans will not spin, no tachometer edges will be produced, and the firmware (NUM_FANS = 2, which raises a run fault if a fan stalls) will abort oven runs with a fan fault.

parsed.summary: The board is otherwise consistent with the specification (power mux, buck, thermocouple channels, heater switch and ESP32 pin usage all trace as described), but the two fan headers J7/J8 appear to have their supply pins reversed: the +12 V rail is wired to pin 1 and ground to pin 2, whereas the specification states the fan-header 12 V pins are pin 2. This would reverse the supply polarity seen by any fan wired per the standard 4-pin pinout, so the fans would not run and the firmware would raise a stall fault.
